about: VSN smart responsive system. Merchants see 3 controls (desktop, tablet, mobile). Every other breakpoint is calculated with CSS clamp()/interpolation between the anchors. An 'Advanced responsive' toggle unlocks a per-breakpoint override for any responsive setting.
why: Duplicating every control for every breakpoint makes the editor unusable and slows the storefront: Elementor reported up to 47% slower frontend load and 15% more memory when it duplicated controls for 3 extra breakpoints (developers.elementor.com, 'The Road to Additional Custom Breakpoints').

breakpoints.label: Small phone 320
breakpoints.default_source: calculated (scale down, never below accessible minimums)

rules: Numeric settings (font size, spacing, gap, radius, icon size, height) interpolate linearly between anchors with clamp(); above 1440 they may scale up to the 2448 value, below 360 they scale down to the 320 value.
Discrete settings (columns, layout, direction, visibility, alignment, image source) step: each breakpoint inherits the nearest larger anchor unless overridden.
Advanced responsive toggle (per element, off by default) exposes overrides for all 9 breakpoints; only overridden values are output as CSS.
Output is CSS custom properties per element instance + one media query per used breakpoint — no JS layout.
Accessibility floors: body text >= 16px on mobile, touch targets >= 24px, tap areas never shrink below 44px for primary actions.
Theme editor previews only desktop and mobile; tablet and other breakpoints are verified in QA with real browser widths (Stage 8).
